problems.title: High-Concurrency Flash Sale Seat Locking
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing the ticketing platform for a concert drop with 100,000 concurrent users. How do you prevent double-booking seats while protecting PostgreSQL from crashing?
constraints: Max seat lock duration is 10 minutes.

dimensions.name: Read/Write Decoupling
dimensions.description: Serving seat map reads from CDN/Redis.

dimensions.name: Atomic Locking Mechanics
dimensions.description: Using SETNX for atomic lock acquiring.

problems.sampleDefense: Decouple seat map reads to Redis. Acquire atomic seat lock using SETNX key user_id NX PX 600000. Process payment asynchronously via Kafka.
commonPitfalls: Querying PostgreSQL directly for seat availability during a drop.

problems.title: Global Multi-Region API Rate Limiter
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are building an API Gateway for a global cloud provider serving 500,000 requests/sec across 3 geographical regions (US, EU, AP). How do you enforce a strict per-user quota of 1,000 req/min with sub-millisecond overhead?

dimensions.name: Local vs Global Counter Sync
dimensions.description: Decoupling per-region local token buckets from global asynchronous reconciliation.

dimensions.name: Atomic Edge Execution
dimensions.description: Using Redis Lua scripts at edge PoPs.

problems.sampleDefense: Deploy local Redis token buckets at each edge region using atomic Lua scripts. Synchronize token usage asynchronously to a global coordinator in batches to avoid cross-region latency on every request.
commonPitfalls: Making synchronous cross-region database calls on every API request.

problems.title: Reliable E-Commerce Order Processing Pipeline
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing the order processing backend for an e-commerce platform during Black Friday. When a customer places an order, 5 downstream services (Inventory, Billing, Shipping, Analytics, Fraud) must process it. How do you ensure high throughput and zero lost orders if Shipping goes down?

dimensions.name: Asynchronous Decoupling
dimensions.description: Publishing OrderPlaced events to Kafka topic instead of blocking HTTP.

dimensions.name: Idempotency & Retry Safety
dimensions.description: Handling duplicate message delivery using idempotent consumer keys.

problems.sampleDefense: Publish OrderPlaced events to a durable Kafka topic with 7-day retention. Each downstream service consumes from its own consumer group. If Shipping fails, its consumer offset pauses while other services continue unimpeded.
commonPitfalls: Chaining synchronous HTTP calls from Payment -> Inventory -> Shipping.

problems.title: Stateful Voice Socket Load Balancer
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing the gateway load balancer for a real-time voice chat application serving 10,000,000 concurrent WebSocket connections. When a backend voice server crashes or scales up, how do you minimize connection drops and avoid server overload?

dimensions.name: Layer 4 vs Layer 7 Selection
dimensions.description: Using L4 Maglev/IPVS for socket throughput and L7 Envoy for HTTP routing.

dimensions.name: Consistent Ring Virtual Nodes
dimensions.description: Using virtual nodes (vnodes) to prevent traffic hotspots.

problems.sampleDefense: Use Layer 4 Maglev consistent hashing for incoming TCP WebSocket handshakes. Use virtual nodes (vnodes=256) per voice server to evenly distribute connections and ensure scaling up or down only migrates 1/N connections.
commonPitfalls: Using simple round-robin which breaks sticky WebSocket sessions.

problems.title: High-Throughput Financial Time-Series Ledger
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are building a crypto transaction ledger storing 2,000,000 write events per second while supporting point-in-time range queries for balance auditing. How do you design the storage engine indexing strategy?

dimensions.name: Storage Engine Selection
dimensions.description: Choosing LSM-Tree with SSTable compaction for write throughput.

dimensions.name: Bloom Filter Read Optimization
dimensions.description: Using Bloom Filters to prevent unnecessary SSTable disk reads.

problems.sampleDefense: Use an LSM-Tree storage engine (RocksDB/Cassandra) for sequential disk write ingestion. Pair each SSTable with an in-memory Bloom Filter to eliminate disk reads for non-existent keys during balance lookups.
commonPitfalls: Using a single B+ Tree PostgreSQL table which locks under 2M writes/sec.

problems.title: Global Multi-Region Distributed Key-Value Store
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing etcd for a global Kubernetes cluster spanning 5 cloud regions. During a cross-continent fiber cut, the cluster partitions into 2 nodes (Region A, B) and 3 nodes (Region C, D, E). How does your consensus protocol prevent split-brain data corruption?
constraints: Network partition isolates 2 nodes from 3 nodes.

dimensions.name: Majority Quorum Enforcement
dimensions.description: Requiring > N/2 (3 of 5) votes for Raft leader election and write commits.

dimensions.name: Minority Partition Behavior
dimensions.description: Rejecting writes on the 2-node minority partition.

problems.sampleDefense: Raft requires majority consensus (> N/2 = 3 nodes). The 3-node partition achieves majority (3/5), elects a leader, and accepts writes. The 2-node minority partition fails to reach quorum and steps down to read-only/error mode, preventing split-brain.
commonPitfalls: Allowing both sides of a network partition to accept writes.

problems.title: Global Multi-Tenant E-Commerce Sharding Engine
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are scaling a SaaS database past 20TB for 50,000 corporate tenants. How do you design a database sharding and query routing layer that eliminates cross-shard joins while preventing tenant hotspots?
constraints: 20TB total database size across 50,000 corporate tenants.

dimensions.name: Tenant Isolation Shard Key Strategy
dimensions.description: Sharding by tenant_id to colocate tenant tables on single physical shards.

dimensions.name: Shard Router Directory Lookup
dimensions.description: Using a low-latency Shard Router with consistent hashing.

problems.sampleDefense: Shard by tenant_id using a dedicated Shard Router service backed by Redis. Colocate all relational tables for a given tenant on the same physical database shard to enable local SQL joins without cross-shard RPC overhead.
commonPitfalls: Sharding different tables on different keys, forcing cross-shard distributed joins.

problems.title: Resilient Webhook Dispatch Pipeline
problems.scenarioPrompt: Your system sends 10,000,000 webhook events daily to external developer endpoints. Merchant receivers frequently drop connections or timeout. How do you design a resilient retry pipeline that handles backpressure and isolates failing merchants?
constraints: Failing merchant endpoints must not stall healthy dispatches.

dimensions.name: Queue Isolation & Backpressure
dimensions.description: Using per-merchant queues and exponential backoff with jitter.

dimensions.name: Dead Letter Queue Routing
dimensions.description: Routing failed messages to DLQ after max retries.

problems.sampleDefense: Use SQS/RabbitMQ message queues with exponential backoff and randomized jitter. Route messages to a Dead Letter Queue after 5 consecutive failures and trip a per-merchant circuit breaker to pause dispatches to unresponsive endpoints.
commonPitfalls: Retrying webhooks synchronously on main worker threads.

problems.title: Third-Party Payment Gateway Resilience Engine
problems.scenarioPrompt: Your e-commerce backend integrates with Stripe and PayPal for payment processing. During a payment partner outage, latency spikes from 200ms to 30 seconds per request, causing app server thread pool exhaustion. How do you protect overall checkout availability?
constraints: App server thread pool size: 200 workers.

dimensions.name: Short-Circuit Fail-Fast Strategy
dimensions.description: Tripping circuit breaker OPEN to instantly fail fast or route to fallback.

dimensions.name: Automatic Failover & Recovery
dimensions.description: Using Half-Open canary probes to test upstream recovery.

problems.sampleDefense: Wrap payment provider SDK calls in a Resilience4j circuit breaker with a 50% failure threshold and 5-second execution timeout. If Stripe times out, trip to OPEN immediately to route checkouts to PayPal fallback.
commonPitfalls: Allowing workers to block for 30 seconds on timing out calls, starving thread pools.

problems.title: Enterprise RAG Knowledge Assistant Architecture
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are building an AI assistant querying 10,000,000 corporate documents with strict per-tenant data isolation. How do you design the vector ingestion, indexing, and RAG retrieval pipeline?

dimensions.name: Metadata Pre-Filtering & Tenant Isolation
dimensions.description: Pre-filtering HNSW vector searches by tenant_id payload.

dimensions.name: Chunking & Quantization
dimensions.description: Using 512-token semantic chunking with scalar quantization.

problems.sampleDefense: Chunk documents into 512-token segments and generate 1536-dim OpenAI embeddings. Store in a Qdrant/Pinecone cluster with pre-filtered HNSW metadata namespace per tenant. Cache frequent prompt context in Redis.
commonPitfalls: Post-filtering tenant boundaries after ANN graph traversal, risking cross-tenant data leakage.

problems.title: Zero-Trust Financial API Security Mesh
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing the security architecture for a banking platform serving 20,000 API requests/sec across 100 internal microservices. How do you implement zero-trust authorization and token revocation?
constraints: Compromised tokens must be revocable within 1 second.

dimensions.name: Stateless JWT Verification & JWKS Cache
dimensions.description: Verifying RS256 JWTs using cached JWKS public keys at API Gateway.

dimensions.name: Redis Revocation Blacklist & mTLS
dimensions.description: Using mTLS for service IPC and Redis bloom filters for token revocation.

problems.sampleDefense: Authenticate external calls at Envoy API Gateway via RS256 JWTs verified against cached JWKS. Maintain a Redis revocation blacklist for revoked JTI IDs. Secure inter-service calls using mTLS certificates issued by SPIFFE/SPIRE.
commonPitfalls: Using symmetric secret keys shared across all 100 microservices.

problems.title: Zero-Downtime Continuous Deployment Pipeline
problems.scenarioPrompt: You are building the deployment engine for a global streaming service executing 100 production deployments daily across 5,000 Kubernetes pods. How do you design an automated Canary analysis and rollback pipeline?
constraints: Automatic rollback trigger latency under 10 seconds.

dimensions.name: Argo Rollouts & Traffic Weighting
dimensions.description: Using Service Mesh / NGINX ingress traffic weighting (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

dimensions.name: Automated Metric Analysis & Rollback
dimensions.description: Comparing Prometheus error rates and p99 latency between canary and baseline.

problems.sampleDefense: Use Argo Rollouts on Kubernetes with Istio service mesh traffic splitting. Shift 2% traffic to canary. Compare Prometheus HTTP 5xx rates against baseline pods every 60 seconds; trigger automatic rollback if errors breach 0.5%.
commonPitfalls: Deploying breaking database schema changes before code expansion phases.

problems.title: Microservice Fault Injection & Quality Gate Architecture
problems.scenarioPrompt: You lead engineering quality for a ride-sharing platform with 2,000 microservices. How do you design a CI/CD contract validation pipeline and automated Chaos Engineering experiment program?
constraints: Chaos experiments must run safely during production hours.

dimensions.name: Pact Broker CI Quality Gate
dimensions.description: Blocking deployments via Pact Broker `can-i-deploy` status check.

dimensions.name: Steady-State Chaos Experiments
dimensions.description: Using Litmus/Chaos Mesh to inject latency and verify steady-state metrics.

problems.sampleDefense: Enforce Pact contract verification in PR build pipelines; block merges using `can-i-deploy`. Run automated Chaos Mesh experiments in production injecting 200ms latency to verify circuit breaker trip thresholds.
commonPitfalls: Running chaos experiments without automated metric rollbacks or steady-state metrics.
